{

    {"value": "12", "meaning": "number of popular open-source Python repositories used in SWE-bench"},
    {"value": "~90,000", "meaning": "total number of pull requests collected from the 12 repositories"},

    {"value": "5888", "meaning": "maximum number of lines edited in a reference patch"},

    {"value": "31", "meaning": "maximum number of files edited in a reference patch"},

  "claims": [
    "SWE-bench is a benchmark of GitHub issues from popular repositories that report bugs or request new features, paired with pull requests that resolve these issues.",
    "The task is to generate a pull request that addresses a given issue and passes tests related to the issue.",
    "SWE-bench uses a 3-stage pipeline: scraping PRs, attribute-based filtering, and execution-based filtering.",
    "The original ~90,000 PRs are filtered down to 2,294 task instances.",
    "Each task instance consists of a large and complex codebase and a description of a relevant issue.",
    "Issue descriptions are typically long and detailed, averaging 195.1 words.",
    "Codebases regularly contain many thousands of files, averaging 3,010 non-test files.",
    "Codebases have an average of 438K non-test lines.",
    "SWE-bench's reference solutions average editing 1.7 files, 3.0 functions, and 32.8 lines.",
    "For each task instance, there is at least one fail-to-pass test used to test the reference solution.",
    "40% of instances have at least two fail-to-pass tests.",
    "A median of 51 additional tests are run to check whether prior functionality is properly maintained.",
    "SWE-bench does not constrain edit scope to an individual function or class, challenging models to generate revisions in multiple locations of a large codebase.",
    "SWE-bench Lite is a subset of 300 instances sampled to be more self-contained, focusing on evaluating functional bug fixes.",
    "SWE-bench Lite covers 11 of the original 12 repositories."
  ]
}
